item.title: Fiji women’s futsal team drawn alongside Senegal, Colombia and Ukraine at Youth Olympics
item.description: Fiji’s young women’s futsal team will face a major challenge at next month’s 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, with head coach Jose Gerardo acknowledging the gap in international experience but backing his players to compete with discipline and determination. Fiji is in Group A alongside Senegal, Colombia and Ukraine, with the top two teams progressing to the semi-finals.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji’s young women’s futsal team will face a major challenge at next month’s 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, with head coach Jose Gerardo acknowledging the gap in international experience but backing his players to compete with discipline and determination.

Fiji is in Group A alongside Senegal, Colombia and Ukraine, with the top two teams progressing to the semi-finals.

Gerardo says the team has been selected after observing players in both outdoor football and indoor futsal, with technique, physical ability, personality, game understanding and attitude all considered during the selection process.

He says the establishment of a national women’s futsal league has also helped provide an opportunity to identify players.

Gerardo says discipline within the squad has been very good, describing his relationship with the players as one based on friendship and respect.

Gerardo says he cannot promise a medal, but the players can promise discipline, attitude and their best effort.

The 2026 Youth Olympic Games will be held in Dakar from October 30 to November 14.

item.title: Defending champions Rewa step up preparations for IDC title defence
item.description: The FMF IDC defending champions are back in training and focused on defending their title after their loss to Rewa in the BOG final. Assistant Coach Priyant Mannu says the team has given the players some time to recover following the BOG final and preparations are now progressing well.
item.content:encoded:
The FMF IDC defending champions are back in training and focused on defending their title after their loss to Rewa in the BOG final.

Assistant Coach Priyant Mannu says the team has given the players some time to recover following the BOG final and preparations are now progressing well.

He says the team has also identified areas that need to be strengthened following the BOG loss, with their game plan being one of the key areas of focus.

Mannu says the team is currently working on the players’ fitness and recovering those carrying injuries to ensure they have the best possible squad going into the IDC.

He says there could be a few changes to the squad that featured in the BOG, with several changes expected as players prepare for the World Cup.

Mannu says the team is also focused on learning from their previous IDC campaign as they look to perform well again this year.

Meanwhile, Team Director and Vice President for Youth Development Amish Patel says says the FMF IDC defending champions are expecting a tougher challenge this year, with the tournament being hosted in the Southern Division.

Patel says Rewa’s pool is strong, with Nasinu, Suva and Labasa all expected to provide a tough challenge.

He is also calling on Rewa fans to support the team at the stadium throughout the tournament.

FMF IDC will be from the 6th to 11th of next month.

item.title: Fijiana one win away from WXV Global Series Challenger title
item.description: The Vodafone Fijiana XV are one win away from claiming the WXV Global Series Challenger 2026 title as they head into the final round this weekend against the Netherlands. Fiji currently sits at the top of the standings with 10 points after securing two bonus-point victories, while the Netherlands are second on nine points and Spain are third on seven.
item.content:encoded:
The Vodafone Fijiana XV are one win away from claiming the WXV Global Series Challenger 2026 title as they head into the final round this weekend against the Netherlands.

Fiji currently sits at the top of the standings with 10 points after securing two bonus-point victories, while the Netherlands are second on nine points and Spain are third on seven.

Only Fiji and the Netherlands remain in contention for the title.

The Fijiana will face the Netherlands in their final match, with the Dutch side having opened their campaign with a 70-0 win over Samoa before producing another strong performance against Brazil.

Fiji, meanwhile, secured a hard-fought 38-32 victory over Spain in the opening round before overcoming Hong Kong China, with their power and attacking skills proving decisive.

The match-up is expected to feature several key battles, including Fijiana players Alfreda Fisher, Adi Salote Nailolo and Varanisese Qoro against the Netherlands’ Linde van der Velden, Kika Mulling and Inger Jongerius.

If the match ends in a draw, Fiji would still claim the title if Spain defeats Brazil with a bonus point.

Fiji would also win the title if the Netherlands earn a four-try bonus point in a draw, as the Fijiana hold the higher world ranking.

The Netherlands-Fiji clash will determine the WXV Global Series Challenger champion, with the Fijiana looking to finish their campaign with the title.

The Fijiana will play the Netherlands Women i n the WXV Global Series final this Saturday at 4pm in Hong Kong. Source: RugbyPass

item.title: Fiji Pearls show positive signs despite missing 2027 World Cup qualification
item.description: The Crest Fiji Pearls have returned home after their campaign at the Netball World Cup Qualifier in Tonga, where they recorded two wins and two losses. The Pearls fell short of securing qualification for the 2027 Netball World Cup in Australia, but head coach Michelle Parsons says there were positive signs from the young side.
item.content:encoded:
The Crest Fiji Pearls have returned home after their campaign at the Netball World Cup Qualifier in Tonga, where they recorded two wins and two losses.

The Pearls fell short of securing qualification for the 2027 Netball World Cup in Australia, but head coach Michelle Parsons says there were positive signs from the young side.

Parsons says several players produced brilliant performances throughout the tournament , with the team continuing to find its rhythm as a developing squad.

She believes the young players will continue to improve with more international exposure and time together as a team.

Parsons had earlier indicated that one of her key goals heading into the Tonga qualifier was to improve Fiji's world ranking and lay the foundation for future World Cup qualification.

With a young squad coming through, Parsons now has time to develop and build a strong and competitive team ahead of the next World Cup qualification campaign.

The tournament in Tonga has also provided valuable international experience for the players as they continue their development and prepare for future competitions.

item.title: Navua focuses on discipline and finishing ahead of FMF IDC
item.description: Navua FC coach Rodeck Singh says the team is focused on improving its discipline and finishing as it prepares for the FMF Inter District Championship. Singh says the team has learned important lessons from its recent BOG campaign and does not want a repeat of what happened during the tournament.
item.content:encoded:
Navua FC coach Rodeck Singh says the team is focused on improving its discipline and finishing as it prepares for the FMF Inter District Championship.

Singh says the team has learned important lessons from its recent BOG campaign and does not want a repeat of what happened during the tournament.

He says discipline will be a major focus, with the team determined not to lose players to red cards, particularly at crucial stages of the tournament.

Singh says the team is also working on its transition play and finishing after missing several scoring opportunities during the BOG.

He says the players are working to sharpen their finishing and ensure they are more clinical in front of goal.

Singh says Navua currently has no major injury concerns and hopes the team remains injury-free throughout the tournament.

He is also calling on Navua supporters to come out in numbers and back the team during the competition.

Navua is in Pool B of the Super Premier Division alongside Ba, Lautoka and Nadi.

The FMF IDC will be held from 6th to 11th October.
